why: The answer has the right pieces: a while loop, StdIn.readInt() inside the body, and printing the value. It breaks Java's scoping rule, though. x is declared inside the loop body but tested in the condition before it exists, so the code won't compile. It also gives no explanation of how the loop gets each new number, and it never handles the stop value 0 correctly. It shows one correct idea (reading inside the loop) without a working loop.
